newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to export six million bpd in five years - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to export six million bpd in five years - paper.

text.p: Iraq has drawn up plans to boost oil exports to six million barrels per day in five years once U.N. trade sanctions are lifted, a senior oil official said in remarks published on Sunday.

"Iraq will have the ability to produce six million bpd within five years from the date the unfair embargo on it is removed," Sami Sahrif, oil ministry undersecretary, told the the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya.

He said Iraq would rely on help from friendly countries to achieve such a production level. He said the pumping of six million bpd would consume three percent a year of Iraq's proven reserves of 114 billion barrels.
Iraq puts its probable reserves at 214 billion barrels.
Iraq has been negotiating with French and Russian firms to develop oilfields in the north and south of the country. It says the firms would start in earnest once sanctions on it are lifted.
The United Nations embargo imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990 bars trade with Baghdad.
The embargo includes a ban on oil exports but the U.N. has allowed Iraq to pump $2 billion worth of oil in six months to international markets on humanitarian grounds.
